# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-7 (Extended v77)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; **Valjean ESCAPES from M. sur M. jail same evening Javert arrested him beside Fantine's death-bed**); December 1823 (Montfermeil tavern, Valjean rescued Cosette, paid Thénardier 1,500 francs); **December 26, 1823 (Valjean and Cosette returned to Paris via Barrier Monceaux)**; 1824 Spring onward (lodging at decrepit building; winter passed; spring advanced); **Summer of second year (approximately 1825-1826)**: Inside walled garden compound, le Petit-Picpus district; sanctuary achieved; **AUTUMN OF SECOND YEAR (Chapter 7 opening—approximately late 1825 or late 1826)**.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles); Dunstead/Kelford/Ravenmere/Staveford (English harbor towns); Arras; Waterloo battlefield; Toulon port; Paris (1823-1826) including Boulevard de l'Hôpital, faubourg Saint-Marceau, Salpêtrière, Porte Saint-Martin, Barrier Monceaux, esplanade of Observatoire, Jardin des Plantes. **Mouffetard quarter** (Rue Censier; Rue Copeau; Rue du Battoir-Saint-Victor; Rue du Puits l'Ermite; Rue de Pontoise; commissary of police office No. 14; Saint-Étienne-du-Mont church). **Gorbeau House (Rue de la Cosette area, Mouffetard quarter)**: Decrepit lodging where Valjean briefly stayed; old woman portress; Javert installed himself, listened at Valjean's door. **Cul-de-Sac de la Planchette**: Location of Pewter Platter tavern (Javert took coach from here to Montfermeil). **Street lantern incident**: Rope cut during Valjean's escape from Mouffetard quarter; Javert found this as sign. **Cul-de-Sac Genrot**: Blind alley with tolerably low walls bordering gardens and waste stretches where Javert conducted fruitless search, believing Valjean fled there. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, walls and solitude; monkish aspect; roads unpaved. **RUE PETIT-PICPUS and RUE DROIT-MUR**: Bordered by mean houses and solitary severe building. **Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (CONVENT CARRIAGE GATE)**: Usually stands ajar; permits view of courtyard surrounded by walls hung with vines; lounging porter visible; tall trees above wall visible at courtyard bottom; when sunlight enlivens courtyard or porter cheered by wine, creates smiling impression despite sombre interior reality. **Wall (approximately 18 feet height)**: Extended from niche angle to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur to gloomy building. **Gloomy building (CONVENT)**: Severe, somber aspect; only one window heavily shuttered with sheet zinc; front has ancient cistern pipes and linden-tree with ivy above wall; interior façades tragic with all windows grated; upper story has scuttles resembling prison cells. **INTERIOR GARDEN (convent grounds)**: Vast oblong area with alley of large poplars at further end; tolerably tall forest trees in corners; unshaded space in centre with large solitary tree, gnarled fruit-trees, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well; stone benches; alleys bordered with gloomy shrubs; grass and green mould covered rest; roof of building descended from wooden barricade top to within short distance of ground with gentle slope grazing linden-tree; wall much higher on garden side; ground at very great depth below. **Interior entry point**: Quadrangular hole about one foot square with grating of interlacing iron bars (black, knotted, solid, forming squares of less than 1.5 inches diagonal); prevented body passage but allowed passage of eyes/mind; re-enforced by sheet of tin inserted in wall rear, pierced with thousand microscopic holes; aperture at bottom similar to letter-box orifice; bit of tape attached to bell-wire hung at right of grated opening.

## Jean Valjean's Current Sanctuary Status (AUTUMN SECOND YEAR)
**ESCAPE FROM M. SUR M.**: Evening of January 1823 when Javert arrested him beside Fantine's death-bed; successfully escaped from town jail; climbed 18-foot wall using muscular force; placed Cosette on back; descended safely to interior garden via roof. **REFUGE DISCOVERY AND FAUCHELEVENT**: Encountered elderly crippled gardener Fauchelevent, admitted to Convent of Petit-Picpus approximately two years previously (1821) on Mayor Madeleine's recommendation after falling from cart; Fauchelevent explained bell-sound as coming from kneecap device worn while spreading straw mats over melon beds. **PSYCHOLOGICAL STATE**: So long as Cosette near him, needs nothing except for her, fears nothing except for her; experiencing continual tremor; distrust of day and night equally. **COSETTE**: Now sleeping in Fauchelevent's bed; rosy; completely dependent on Valjean. **CURRENT LOCATION AUTUMN YEAR 2**: Still secured in convent sanctuary (Convent of Petit-Picpus, Quartier Saint-Antoine); wearing cravat and coat; hat recovered. **VALJEAN'S ALTERED APPEARANCE**: Sadness, uneasiness, anxiety, depression from forced nighttime flight, regulating pace to child's pace—all this has altered Valjean's walk and impressed senility on his bearing such that police themselves (Javert) made mistake in doubting his identity. Costume of émigré preceptor, Thénardier's declaration making him grandfather, belief in his death in prison—all added to uncertainty in Javert's mind.

## Javert's Pursuit and Strategic Hesitation (CRITICAL DEVELOPMENT—EXTENDED)
**REASSIGNMENT TO PARIS**: When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail (January 1823), police supposed he went to Paris; Javert summoned to assist; his zeal and intelligence remarked by M. Chabouillet, secretary of Prefecture under Comte Anglès; Javert (already Chabouillet's patron) attached to Paris police force circa 1823. **NEWSPAPER REPORT**: December 1823, newspaper announced Jean Valjean's death in formal terms; Javert read name, remarked "That's a good entry," threw paper aside, thought no more. **REACTIVATION**: Police report from Seine-et-Oise prefecture concerning abduction of child Cosette in Montfermeil; Javert's memory revived—recalled Fantine's name, remembered Valjean asked three-day respite to fetch her child, remembered Valjean arrested in Paris stepping into coach for Montfermeil; suspected Valjean had made previous excursion seeking Fantine's daughter; understood: Fantine's daughter in Montfermeil, Valjean seeking her, child stolen by stranger—could stranger be Valjean? But Valjean was dead. **JAVERT'S SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach from Pewter Platter tavern (Cul-de-Sac de la Planchette) to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; got old woman portress talking—she confirmed coat-lined-with-millions episode and thousand-franc bill; hired room, installed himself evening same day; listened at mysterious lodger's door hoping catch voice; Valjean saw candle through key-hole, foiled spy by silence. **REASONS FOR SECRECY (Three Motives)**: (1) slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) to recapture ex-convict reputed dead, classified as most dangerous malefactor, was magnificent success—old Parisian police would not leave to newcomer Javert, feared being deprived of convict; (3) Javert, being artist, had taste for unforeseen—hated well-heralded successes talked of in advance with bloom brushed off; preferred elaborating masterpieces in dark, unveiling suddenly at last. **PURSUIT ESCALATION**: On following day Valjean noticed five-franc piece falling; old woman heard rattling coin, suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; at night when Valjean came out, Javert waited behind trees with two men. **ESCAPE FROM MOUFFETARD**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder in lantern—precious sign which led him astray, turning researches toward Cul-de-Sac Genrot (blind alley with tolerably low walls bordering gardens and waste stretches); explored gardens and waste stretches as hunting for needle; had he penetrated further in Cul-de-Sac Genrot, probably would have caught Valjean and been lost. **JAVERT'S HESITATION AND PSYCHOLOGICAL TORMENT**: Javert followed Valjean from tree to tree, corner to corner, had not lost sight of him for single instant; even when Valjean believed himself most secure, Javert's eye upon him. Why had not Javert arrested Valjean? Because he was still in doubt. **STRATEGIC CALCULATION**: Considered abrupt demand for papers risky—if man was not Valjean, and was honest old fellow living on income, probably some merry blade deeply and cunningly implicated in Parisian misdeeds, chief of dangerous band giving alms to conceal talents (old dodge); had trusty fellows, accomplices' retreats in emergencies; all street turns indicated not simple honest man; to arrest too hastily would be "to kill the hen that laid the golden eggs." Where inconvenience in waiting? Javert very sure man would not escape. **PSYCHOLOGICAL TORMENT**: Began the game—experienced ecstatic and infernal moment; allowed man to go on ahead, knowing had him safe, but desiring postponing moment of arrest as long as possible, happy at thought he was taken yet seeing him free, gloating with gaze with voluptuousness of spider allowing fly to flutter, of cat letting mouse run; claws and talons possess monstrous sensuality; obscure movements of creature imprisoned in their pincers; what delight this strangling is! **MOMENT OF LOSS**: Even at moment when saw Valjean had escaped him, Javert did not lose head; sure convict could not be far off, established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades, beat the quarter all that night. **IMPEDIMENT TO ARREST**: Free press embarrassed police; several arbitrary arrests denounced by newspapers echoed as far as Chambers, rendered Prefecture timid; interference with individual liberty grave matter; police agents afraid of mistakes; prefect laid blame; mistake meant dismissal. Paragraph of grandfather with white hair arrested as escaped convict would have caused effect in Paris—would have been reproduced by twenty newspapers.

## English Harbor Towns Communities (SECONDARY SETTING)
Named residents include: Matho Stenson (watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly; laughed at story nobody else found funny); Ismira Stenson (fell asleep in chair before fire caught); Pelde Stenson (counted coins twice, came up penny short; read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints); Harine Lindmere (watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Davus Stenworth and Havus Stenworth (remarked river up, water swelling in spring; talked of weather, harvest, lame horse); Yera (read almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints); Orrald the Younger and Orrald Stenson (received confidence/gave solemn promise to carry sealed letter to Ravenmere, swore to teach children of Elmhaven letters; bought ribbon, regretted it).

## Fauchelevent (Elderly Gardener—Established Ally)
**Identity**: Old crippled gardener; admitted to Convent of Petit-Picpus approximately two years previously (1821) on recommendation of Mayor Madeleine (Valjean) after falling from cart; now works as gardener in convent grounds. **Character**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; reproaches Valjean for not recognizing him, calls him "Father Madeleine," accuses him of ingratitude despite saving lives; speaks freely about work and circumstances. **Current occupation**: Spreading straw mats over melon beds in garden; wears bell and kneecap device marking movements; bell tinkles with approach and retreat, ceases when halts. **Hospitality**: Provided Cosette safe bed; offered Valjean cheese, black bread, wine; warming themselves at table in his quarters. **Status**: Valjean's only known ally and protector in Paris; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's presence in convent sanctuary.
